```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(knitr)
s <- read.csv("simulation_summary.csv", check.names = FALSE)
get_result <- function(scenario, method, term = "Connectivity", column = "mean") {
  x <- s[s$scenario == scenario & s$method == method & s$term == term, column]
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1)
  x
}
f <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
pct <- function(x) paste0(f(100 * x, 1), "%")
bridge <- read.csv("likelihood_bridge_checks.csv")
joint <- read.csv("joint_gaussian_example.csv")
stopifnot(all(s$attempts == 400), all(s$failures == 0))
```

## Overview: Where Does Per-Trial M-MOMS Succeed, and Where Are Its Boundaries?

In [Step 6 (`decon_connectivity_repair()`)](../medusa_step6_connectivity/medusa_step6_connectivity.qmd), MEDuSA adapts the REPAIR measurement-error framework (Vig & Hallquist, 2026; Fuller, 1987) to trial-level functional connectivity and psychophysiological interaction (PPI): it subtracts per-trial seed measurement variance (`se_demixed^2`) from $X^\top X$, subtracts task-free cross-parcel error covariance (`shared_error = "auto"`) from $X^\top Y$, guards against ill-conditioned denominators via step-up regularization (`method = "mmoms"`), and pools participant slopes using finite-sample Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman (HKSJ) $t$-intervals.

A mathematically minded colleague or reviewer may push one layer deeper: *Per-trial M-MOMS treats each trial's measurement error as additive around an unblurred latent truth ($\mathbb{E}[\widehat{z} \mid \theta] = \theta$). What happens in extreme fMRI regimes where (1) seed and target parcels undergo unequal temporal smoothing ($K_S \neq K_T$), (2) observation errors correlate across consecutive trials ($\Omega_{SS}, \Omega_{ST}$ non-diagonal), or (3) sample sizes drop to $S = 12$ participants?*

::: {.callout-note}
### Core Methodological Question & Connection to the Pipeline
*What are the exact mathematical conditions required for unbiased, nominal-coverage latent connectivity and PPI inference—and how do those conditions explain both Step 6's design choices (`shared_error = "auto"`, `use_whitened = FALSE`, HKSJ pooling) and its scope limits?*

This chapter develops the full cross-trial measurement-error theory extending [**Step 6 (`decon_connectivity_repair()`)**](../medusa_step6_connectivity/medusa_step6_connectivity.qmd) and tests three frontier measurement models across 400-replicate paired stress simulations.
:::

---

## 1. The Full Trial-Vector Measurement Interface

For participant $s \in \{1, \dots, S\}$ and trial $i \in \{1, \dots, m_s\}$, recall the latent within-person connectivity and PPI structural equation from Step 6 with centered task modulator $x_{si}$:

$$
\theta_{T,si} = \alpha_s + \beta_S \theta_{S,si} + \beta_x x_{si} + \beta_P (x_{si}\theta_{S,si}) + \eta_{si},
$$

where $\beta_S$ is baseline seed–target coupling at $x_{si} = 0$, $\beta_x$ absorbs direct task activation in the target region ([Cole et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6422749/)), and $\beta_P$ is task-modulated PPI coupling.

Stacking all $m_s$ trials of participant $s$ into column vectors reveals the **complete linear measurement relationship** produced by deconvolution and epoch readout:

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \widehat{z}_{S,s} \\ \widehat{z}_{T,s} \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} K_{S,s} & 0 \\ 0 & K_{T,s} \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} \theta_{S,s} \\ \theta_{T,s} \end{bmatrix}
+
\begin{bmatrix} u_s \\ v_s \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\!\begin{pmatrix} u_s \\ v_s \end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
\Omega_{SS,s} & \Omega_{ST,s} \\
\Omega_{ST,s}^\top & \Omega_{TT,s}
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Writing the interface in block matrix form makes three structural properties transparent at a glance:

1. **Mean resolution ($K_{S,s}, K_{T,s}$) vs. noise covariance ($\Omega$):** Subtracting error variances $\Omega_{SS,s}$ and $\Omega_{ST,s}$ removes bias caused by random observation noise $(u_s, v_s)$, which yields exact consistency whenever Step 3 demixing restores $K_{S,s} \approx I$ and $K_{T,s} \approx I$. If strong regularization or unmodeled HRF mismatch leaves $K_{S,s} \neq K_{T,s}$ (for instance, a heavily smoothed low-SNR seed predicting a sharp high-SNR target), variance subtraction alone cannot undo the mismatch in deterministic resolution.
2. **Non-commutativity of smoothing/whitening and PPI products:** Notice that multiplying a linearly transformed seed vector $K \theta_S$ elementwise by the task vector $x$ is *not* equal to transforming the latent interaction $\operatorname{diag}(x)\theta_S$:
   $$
   K\,\operatorname{diag}(x)\theta_S \neq \operatorname{diag}(x)\,K\theta_S.
   $$
   The exact same non-commutativity applies to separate parcel ZCA whitening matrices ($T_S \neq T_T$), which is why `decon_connectivity_repair()` defaults to **`use_whitened = FALSE`** so `Seed`, `Target`, and `Seed:x` remain in matched run-centered trial coordinates.
3. **Trial-level vs. participant-level inference units:** Even after unbiased moment subtraction within each participant, off-diagonal serial entries in $\Omega_{SS,s}$ and $\Omega_{TT,s}$ make trial-level score contributions correlated within a scan. Treating pooled rows as independent understates uncertainty, whereas clustering or pooling at the **participant level** respects the true independent sampling unit.

---

## 2. Three Exact Routes When Moving Beyond Diagonal Per-Trial M-MOMS

When rapid event schedules or low regional SNR push $K_S$ and $K_T$ away from the identity matrix, three principled measurement models characterize what can and cannot be recovered:

### Route A: Unpenalized likelihood-only readouts in a full-rank trial basis

Suppose each parcel $g$'s run BOLD vector follows a finite $m$-trial forward design $y_g = G_g \theta_g + Z_g \gamma_g + \varepsilon_g$ under its cross-fitted HRF, and the trial spacing keeps $G_g$ full column rank. Fitting unpenalized generalized least squares in whitened coordinates yields linear trial readouts $\widehat{z}_g = B_g y_g$ satisfying **exact identity resolution**:

$$
B_g G_g = I_m
\quad \Longrightarrow \quad
\mathbb{E}(\widehat{z}_g \mid \theta_g) = \theta_g,
\qquad \Omega_{gg} = B_g \Sigma_g B_g^\top,
\qquad \Omega_{ST} = B_S \Sigma_{\varepsilon_S, \varepsilon_T} B_T^\top.
$$

This route is the exact fMRI analog of REPAIR's likelihood-only OLS stage-1 score reconstruction (Vig & Hallquist, 2026; [Abdulrahman & Henson, 2016](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4692520/)). In our numerical verification (`likelihood_only_bridge.R`: 16 events over 180 volumes, distinct regional HRFs, shared serial $\text{AR}$ noise), $B_g G_g = I$ holds to **`r format(max(bridge$value[1:2]), scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`**, and a 10,000-draw Monte Carlo audit matches analytical trial SDs within **`r pct(bridge$value[7])`**. Its practical boundary is collinearity: at sub-2-second jitter or when unmodeled sustained intervals occur between events, unpenalized $G_g$ becomes ill-conditioned—motivating Step 2–3's mildly regularized demixing ($K_g \approx I$).

### Route B: Subspace de-penalization on identifiable contrasts

In continuous TR-grid deconvolution ($T_r = 180$ latent timepoints), a Bayesian/penalized posterior precision takes the form $C_{\text{post}}^{-1} = J + P_{\text{prior}}$. Can we subtract $P_{\text{prior}}$ globally on the TR grid? No: in `likelihood_only_bridge.R`, the 180-column Toeplitz convolution operator has numerical rank **`r f(bridge$value[5], 0)`** because the HRF acts as a low-pass filter. Unshrinking is mathematically well-posed *only* after projecting onto lower-dimensional trial or window subspaces where Fisher information $J$ is nonsingular—precisely what Step 3's target demixing operator $W_\tau$ performs at target event times.

### Route C: Retaining $K_S$ and $K_T$ explicitly in a joint latent Gaussian model

When regional SNR is so low that any inverse $(K_S)^{-1}$ explodes variance, $K_S$ and $K_T$ can instead be kept *forward* inside a joint Gaussian marginal likelihood over $(\widehat{z}_{S,s}, \widehat{z}_{T,s}) \mid x_s$. In `joint_gaussian_demo.R` under deliberately mismatched resolution ($K_S \neq K_T$) and known $\Omega$, joint maximum likelihood recovers connectivity **`r f(joint$estimate[1])`** (truth `0.550`) and PPI **`r f(joint$estimate[3])`** (truth `0.350`), trading parametric Gaussian latent priors and numerical optimization for exact resolution invariance.

<details>
<summary>Gaussian conditional-expectation calibration note</summary>

If one substitutes Empirical-Bayes shrunken seed predictions $m_S = \mathbb{E}(\theta_S \mid \widehat{z}_S, x)$ into a target regression (`eb_predictor` intuition), non-identity target resolution $K_T$ and shared cross-parcel error $\Omega_{TS}$ require transformed regressors $K_T m_S$ and $K_T\operatorname{diag}(x)m_S$ (not $\operatorname{diag}(x)K_T m_S$) together with an explicit shared-noise control term $\Omega_{TS}(K_S V_S K_S^\top + \Omega_{SS})^{-1}(\widehat{z}_S - K_S \mu_S)$.

</details>

---

## 3. Full Cross-Trial Corrected-Score Estimating Equations

When source resolution is approximately unbiased ($K_S \approx K_T \approx I$) while trial errors correlate serially across adjacent events ($\Omega_{SS,s}, \Omega_{ST,s}$ non-diagonal), we can generalize per-trial M-MOM to a **full cross-trial corrected score** ([Nakamura, 1990](https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/77/1/127/271070); [Buonaccorsi, 1996](https://academic.oup.com/biomet/article-abstract/83/2/433/289324)). Letting $\widehat{X}_s = X_s + U_s$ collect participant $s$'s centered `[Seed, x, Seed:x]` matrix and setting $\Psi_s = \mathbb{E}(U_s^\top U_s \mid x_s)$ and $c_s = \mathbb{E}(U_s^\top v_s \mid x_s)$ from the full $m_s \times m_s$ matrices $(\Omega_{SS,s}, \Omega_{ST,s})$, each participant contributes a zero-mean estimating equation:

$$
q_s(\beta) = \widehat{X}_s^\top \widehat{z}_{T,s} - c_s - \bigl(\widehat{X}_s^\top \widehat{X}_s - \Psi_s\bigr)\beta,
\qquad \sum_{s=1}^S q_s(\widehat{\beta}) = 0,
$$

with participant-cluster sandwich covariance:

$$
\widehat{V}_{\text{cluster}} = H^{-1}\left[\frac{S}{S - 1}\sum_{s=1}^S q_s(\widehat{\beta}) q_s(\widehat{\beta})^\top\right]H^{-\top},
\qquad H = \sum_{s=1}^S \bigl(\widehat{X}_s^\top \widehat{X}_s - \Psi_s\bigr).
$$

---

## 4. Stress-Test Benchmarks: Shared Noise, Serial Errors, Unequal $K$, and Small $S$

To see exactly what each modeling ingredient buys—and what fails when an ingredient is omitted—we evaluate 400 paired Monte Carlo cohorts per scenario ($S = 60$ participants, or $S = 12$ in `Few participants`; 24 trials/participant; true $\beta_S = 0.55$, $\beta_x = 0.25$, $\beta_P = 0.35$, or $\beta_S = \beta_P = 0$ under `Null`; serial trial error correlation $0.55$; shared cross-parcel error correlation $0.45$, under both Gaussian and heavy-tailed $t_5$ errors):

![Mean coefficient bias across three stress regimes (`Shared / serial Gaussian`, `Shared / serial t5`, and `Different resolution` where $K_S \neq K_T$). Horizontal intervals show $\pm 1.96$ Monte Carlo SEs. Subtracting full cross-trial and cross-parcel error moments eliminates bias under both Gaussian and heavy-tailed $t_5$ serial/shared noise, whereas unequal deterministic resolution ($K_S \neq K_T$) requires inverting or modeling $K$ (`Undo K + full`).](bias.png){#fig-bias width="100%" fig-alt="Faceted dot-and-interval plot of connectivity and PPI bias across seven estimators and three stress scenarios."}

![Empirical coverage of nominal 95% confidence intervals across the same three stress regimes (exact Clopper–Pearson 95% intervals around empirical coverage; dashed vertical line marks 95%). Notice that under serial trial errors, row-level SEs (`Full + row SE`) undercover on main connectivity even when point estimates are unbiased, whereas participant-cluster SEs (`Full + cluster SE`) achieve 95% coverage.](coverage.png){#fig-coverage width="100%" fig-alt="Faceted dot-and-interval plot of 95% CI coverage across seven estimators and three stress scenarios."}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-conn-benchmarks
#| tbl-cap: "Selected conditional connectivity and PPI stress-test benchmarks (400 paired replications per row; true Connectivity = 0.550, true PPI = 0.350)."
#| echo: false
show <- s[s$method %in% c("Full moments, cluster SE", "Resolution inverse + full moments") &
  s$scenario %in% c("Serial + shared Gaussian", "Serial + shared t5", "Different resolution", "Few participants"), ]
show <- show[order(show$scenario, show$method, show$term), ]
kable(
  data.frame(
    Scenario = show$scenario,
    Estimator = show$method,
    Term = show$term,
    Mean = round(show$mean, 3),
    Bias = round(show$bias, 3),
    `95% Coverage` = pct(show$coverage),
    `Coverage MCSE` = pct(show$coverage_mcse),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## 5. Implications for Applied Step 6 Connectivity Analyses

Every result in @fig-bias, @fig-coverage, and @tbl-conn-benchmarks explains a specific design rule in `decon_connectivity_repair()`:

1. **Why `shared_error = "auto"` is essential (never strip cross-parcel noise metadata):** In @fig-bias (`Shared / serial Gaussian` and `t5`), subtracting seed variance *without* subtracting shared seed–target error covariance (`No shared error` and `Diagonal moments`) severely over-estimates main connectivity, and under `Null serial + shared` falsely rejects the null in **`r pct(get_result("Null serial + shared", "Zero shared covariance", column = "rejection"))`** of cohorts—compared with **`r pct(get_result("Null serial + shared", "Full moments, cluster SE", column = "rejection"))`** once $\Omega_{ST}$ is subtracted. Always pass the `subject_epochs` list (or `.rds`/Parquet panels retaining `shared_noise_loading`) into `decon_connectivity_repair()`.
2. **Why `decon_connectivity_repair()` pools participant slopes with HKSJ $t$-intervals:** In @fig-coverage, treating correlated trials as independent rows (`Full + row SE`) drops connectivity coverage to **`r pct(get_result("Serial + shared Gaussian", "Full moments, row SE", column = "coverage"))`**, while participant-cluster SEs restore **`r pct(get_result("Serial + shared Gaussian", "Full moments, cluster SE", column = "coverage"))`** at $S = 60$—yet asymptotic normal cluster $z$-intervals still drop to **`r pct(get_result("Few participants", "Full moments, cluster SE", column = "coverage"))`** at $S = 12$ ([MacKinnon, Nielsen & Webb, 2022](https://arxiv.org/html/2205.03285v1)). Fitting M-MOMS within each participant and pooling across participants via HKSJ $t$-intervals anchors degrees of freedom to $S - 1$ even in modest neuroimaging cohorts.
3. **Why seed and target smoothing policies should match ($K_S \approx K_T$):** Under `Different resolution`, variance disattenuation alone overshoots connectivity (`r f(get_result("Different resolution", "Full moments, cluster SE"))` vs. truth `0.550`), whereas inverting well-conditioned resolution operators (`Undo K + full`) restores **`r f(get_result("Different resolution", "Resolution inverse + full moments"))`**. In empirical studies, keep Step 2–3 regularization and demixing settings matched across seed and target parcels (`demix_target_trials = TRUE`, `use_whitened = FALSE`) and inspect `diagnose_crossrun_recovery()` self-gain in both regions before interpreting asymmetric seed–target slopes.
